THE VERIFICATION WORKBENCH

Trust starts with a check you can repeat.

Sign a receipt. Change one field. Challenge a signer. Follow a policy version. Six small experiments make the evidence mechanisms visible and inspectable.

The verification code runs locally on synthetic inputs. These demonstrations establish bounded properties under their verifiers; they do not provide production runtime enforcement or certify an agent.

SIX EXPERIMENTS · SYNTHETIC INPUTS

Run a check, challenge it, and inspect the underlying artifact. Each panel uses the published verification modules in your browser. An intact signature establishes integrity; trusted identity and deployment authority require separate evidence.

01 · Signatures
02 · Batches
03 · Policy history
04 · Configuration
05 · Delegation
06 · Authority

01 · SIGNATURE INTEGRITY

Flip one byte and it voids.

Sign a synthetic score receipt with ECDSA P-256 in your browser (Web Crypto — the private key never leaves this page), then verify it offline with only the attestation itself. Then try to cheat.

Sign + verify
Tamper with it
Wrong signer

Integrity + authenticity only: it proves the content is intact and this key signed it — not that the key belongs to a real-world identity. That binding is a separate PKI/attestation concern.

02 · BATCH INCLUSION

Eight receipts. One signature. Each provable alone.

Batch eight synthetic receipts into a Merkle tree, sign only the root, then prove one receipt's inclusion without revealing the others. Leaves are beneficiary-bound and domain-separated (leaf: vs node:) against second-preimage games.

Batch + sign the root
Tamper a receipt
Re-point the beneficiary

03 · POLICY HISTORY

Yesterday's decision, judged by yesterday's policy.

A policy is not a mutable blob — it's a hash-chained sequence of versions, and every decision binds to the exact version it ran under. Amend the policy all you like; you can't retroactively make a past decision look compliant.

Build the history + bind a decision
Rewrite history

04 · CONFIGURATION BINDING

Change the configuration. Re-check the evidence.

Evaluate a synthetic policy against the deterministic IAM battery, inspect its config-bound credential, then change the declared model. No named agent is contacted or executed.

Issue a reference check
Run the allow-all baseline
Drift the config
Download the credential
Copy a /verify link

This credential records reproducible policy behavior under this verifier + this config. It is an unsigned, digest-bound synthetic example, not a permission grant or certification. Real design-partner evidence stays blocked until authorized.

Run your own reference check →

05 · DELEGATED AUTHORITY

Widen one edge. Watch the root's blast radius move.

A correct capability token can only narrow as it is delegated, so an ancestor reaches exactly its own grant. Break that on any edge and authority flows back up the tree.

platform
ops
finance
payroll-bot
pii-bot
ledger-bot
Widen payroll-bot
Widen pii-bot
Widen ledger-bot
PASS
attenuation holds — Every child narrows. The root reaches exactly its own grant: 5 of 9 sensitive resources.
NOTE
blast radius at the root — 5 / 9 sensitive resources reachable — BRI 55.6%

06 · AUTHORITY ANALYSIS

Inspect the authority that goes unused.

Compare granted and exercised authority across a seeded synthetic fleet. Inspect five metrics with stated denominators, widen one delegation edge, or measure detection against planted ground truth.

Analyze the fleet
Widen one delegation edge
Score against planted ground truth

The corpus is SYNTHETIC and seeded — these numbers measure the analyzer, not any real deployment, and no claim is made about any customer's authorization data. The published artifact re-derives byte-for-byte from its seed; definitions, denominators, and limits are in docs/OVER-GRANT-METRICS.md.
